aboutAuthor: Saurabh Mukherjea founded Marcellus Investment Managers and writes on Indian equities. He hunts for greatness defined as decade-long fifteen percent ROCE with revenue growth every year.

points.heading: Greatness is rare and measurable
points.body: Only seven of 3,900 firms meet ten-year fifteen percent ROCE plus growing sales every year. Coffee can portfolios built on that filter turned Rs 100 into Rs 100,000 while churning failed.

points.heading: IBAS names the moat
points.body: Innovation, Brands, Architecture, and Strategic Assets form a diamond where at least one corner must be defensible — Asian Paints in architecture, HDFC in CASA, Astral in technology alliance.

points.heading: Distribution discipline over product hype
points.body: Dealer tinting, plumber training, and farmer procurement create negative working capital and loyalty that fund growth without debt, unlike leveraged peers who collapse.

points.heading: Read rating reports before annual reports
points.body: Agencies flag promoter pledges, related-party, and cash-flow mismatches that glossy annual letters hide. Checking them first prevents seduction by narrative.

points.heading: Hold, don't churn
points.body: After-tax churn drag of five percent annually destroys six percent CAGR versus buy-and-hold. Greatness rewards boredom, checklist patience, and selling only when IBAS breaks.

points.heading: Contrarian pricing is temporary
points.body: HDFC and Axis were dismissed as expensive or troubled; their architecture and CASA proved durable while sceptics overweighted headlines. Price follows moat, not consensus.

insights: Rajdhani Express observation that evolved into 0.5 percent greatness filter and Rs 100 to Rs 100,000 coffee can chart.
Wald-style survivorship lesson: admire bullet holes you see, but armor engine zones where failed firms never return to tell tale.
Credit rating report eleven-question checklist that catches self-sustainable growth breaches before auditor notes do.
conclusion: The Unusual Billionaires argues that durable compounding is scarce, checklist-identifiable via ROCE and IBAS, and profitable only when held boringly without churning through every market story that tempts activity.
